specDepartures.spec: Acceptance bullet 4: 'Bus reachable but refusing the publish: the same 503 and the same record, carrying the bus's own reason'; and 'A publish the bus refuses outright is answered the same way'.
specDepartures.plan: A publish the NATS server denies under this listener's own permissions answers 403, no Retry-After, body 'envoy: the message bus denied the publish under this listener's own permissions: <reason>', outcome publish_denied (api.go refuseBusUnavailable / publishDeniedPrefix). Only the publish route, for a topic the stream does not capture, can get it. A refusal from the stream itself keeps the 503 with the bus's reason.
specDepartures.evidence: Review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-r5h; packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts retries every status >= 500, so a 503 sends the client back to a denial that cannot succeed. Tests: cmd/listener TestADeniedPublishIsRefusedPermanentlyAndNotRecordedAsBusUnavailable; internal/bus TestPublishCoreReportsAPublishNATSDenies, TestAnAdHocPublishNATSDeniesReturnsTheDenial. No Dispatch record of the human approving the acceptance change; spec approval is still v10.

outcome.scope: acceptance: spec bullet 4 ('Bus reachable but refusing the publish') — a grant denial is 403, not 503

specDepartures.spec: 'A message the delivery path still cannot place is retried rather than thrown away, for at most one minute, and then given up and counted.'
specDepartures.plan: At most unplaceableDeferralCap (consumerMaxAckPending/4 = 64) messages are held deferred per listener at once, in one set shared by every handler. A message that finds the cap full is given up and counted on its first delivery, with no retry.
specDepartures.evidence: delivery.go unplaceableDeferralCap and the take() fall-through to the give-up; without it, deferred messages hold the durable's 256 MaxAckPending slots and stall every topic. Tests: TestUnplaceableDeferralsStopAtTheirCap, TestUnplaceableRetryWindowFitsTheBoundsItDependsOn.

outcome.scope: design: the spec's second 'What would close it' point — beyond 64 held messages, an unplaceable message is given up at once rather than retried

specDepartures.spec: 'for at most one minute' of retrying (bullet 5: 'gives the message up after at most a minute of retrying'); how the retry is bounded is the plan's to settle.
specDepartures.plan: The window buys window/5 s deferrals (12 by default) counted from the first delivery (NumDelivered), with a hard stop at 18 deliveries. Handler time (up to 2 s store read per delivery) and AckWait-expired deliveries are not timed, so the worst case from first delivery to give-up is about 86 s [inference from constants]; time a message spent in the stream before its first delivery is not counted.
specDepartures.evidence: delivery.go unplaceableRetryDelay, deliverySessionReadTimeout, unplaceableMaxDeliveries and the window comment; review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-r5c moved the clock from stream age to first delivery so a backlog replayed into a cold listener is not given up at once.
